Percepto launches hardware-agnostic Axion inspection platform

The software combines drone, sensor and historical imagery to prioritize anomalies and answer asset-related questions.

Percepto ↗27 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 5Videos 2

Software independent of the drone stack

Percepto launched Axion SaaS on October 27, describing it as immediately available for third-party drone and sensor data as well as existing imagery. Customers need not buy a Percepto drone to begin analysis. Ranger and the Harbor station remain options for new data collection.

From imagery to decisions

Axion links observations with asset context and history. Percepto cites over 160 AI models developed from more than 100,000 hours of autonomous inspection, with expert validation. It prioritizes anomalies and supports natural-language questions; training experience is not an accuracy score.

Commercial and operating disclosures

Percepto also announced a multi-year extension with an unnamed US energy-transmission customer, without contract value, while moving to consolidate engineering and production in the US. Axion pricing and independent comparisons across anomaly types are not supplied. Operators still need asset-specific evaluation.
